_citation: Dalzell, McArdle, Berta, Bienias, Chen, Gilyén, Hann, Kastoryano, Khabiboulline, Kubica, Salton, Wang, Brandão. 'Quantum algorithms: A survey of applications and end-to-end complexities.' arXiv:2310.03011 (2023). 337 pages.
_version: Dalzell arXiv:2310.03011 v1 (2023-10-05); MSA values pinned to v1 figures and not refreshed against post-2023 algorithmic improvements (see dalzell_framework.md caveats).
_methodology: Dalzell gives PER-APPLICATION logical-qubit and T-count estimates grounded in end-to-end resource analyses. For each silo, we record a 'minimum scale for advantage' (MSA) — below that scale the problem is classically trivial; at/above that scale Dalzell considers the quantum resources to be competitive with the best classical methods.

derivative-pricing._sources: Section 8.2 Monte Carlo methods: Option pricing. Based on Chakrabarti et al. 2021 autocallable/TARF benchmarks and Stamatopoulos 2022 QSP follow-up.
derivative-pricing.target_clock_rate_label: 50 MHz logical clock for wall-clock competitiveness with classical MC (1-10 s)
derivative-pricing.notes: Three sets of estimates available: Chakrabarti autocallable (8k qubits, 1.2e10 T), TARF (12k qubits, 9.8e9 T), QSP-polished (4.7k qubits, 2.4e9 T). We use the most optimistic (QSP) as the MSA floor.

simulation-monte-carlo._sources: Section 8.2 (option pricing is the canonical MC use case in finance)
simulation-monte-carlo.notes: Same MSA as derivative pricing; both are QAE-on-MC.

risk-management._sources: Section 8 mentions VaR/CVaR/CVA (Woerner-Egger 2019; Han-Rebentrost 2022; Stamatopoulos 2022 quantum gradient for Greeks). Resource requirements similar to derivative pricing MC.
risk-management.notes: Greeks / VaR require gradient estimation on top of MC, pushing resources slightly higher than plain option pricing.

portfolio-optimization._sources: Section 22 QIPM for SOCP, Dalzell et al. 2022 resource analysis.
portfolio-optimization.speedup_type: sub-quadratic (QIPM is strictly less than quadratic)
portfolio-optimization.notes: For n=500, m=400 SOCP instance — which classical solvers handle in seconds. Dalzell flags this as a case where the QRAM + QLSS overhead kills any speedup. Effectively infeasible under current end-to-end estimates.

quantum-ml-finance._sources: Dalzell explicitly defers QML-in-finance to reviews; does NOT give end-to-end numbers. Uses the generic QML Section 13.
quantum-ml-finance.notes: Dalzell provides no end-to-end estimate for QML. Many QML proposals (QSVM, Gaussian process regression, low-rank PCA) are dequantized by Tang 2019 / GST 2022. Flagged as insufficient_data unless the specific sub-problem matches a Dalzell-analyzed primitive.

fraud-detection._sources: Not a Dalzell application area. Typically treated as QML.
fraud-detection.notes: Not analyzed. Emit not_applicable unless algorithm is a generic QML primitive.

credit-lending._sources: CVA falls under derivative pricing in Dalzell's taxonomy. Credit scoring is QML.
credit-lending.notes: Use risk-management thresholds (CVA is a risk measure).

cryptography-security._sources: Section 6.1 Breaking cryptosystems. RSA-2048 Shor factoring (Gidney-Ekerå 2021 [10]): ~6000 logical qubits, ~3×10⁹ non-Clifford gates (Toffoli+T), 14000 logical qubits after routing. ECC-256 ECDLP (Ref [27]): 6000 logical qubits, 1.1×10⁸ Toffoli. Grover on AES: 3000-7000 logical, 10^25+ T-gates.
cryptography-security.notes: RSA-2048 via Gidney-Ekerå: 0.3n³ ≈ 3×10⁹ non-Clifford gates for n=2048. ECC-256 is cheaper at 1.1×10⁸ Toffoli. Grover on AES is far worse (10^25+). We use RSA-2048 as the MSA floor since it is the most commonly cited cryptanalysis target.

insurance-actuarial._sources: Not explicitly analyzed. Closest analog is risk-management (tail probabilities via QAE).
insurance-actuarial.notes: Treated as risk-management: actuarial tail estimation is QAE on MC.

simulation-electronic-structure._sources: Section 6 electronic structure, Section 7 quantum chemistry. Von Burg 2021: ~2000 logical qubits, 1e10 Toffoli for FeMoCo.
simulation-electronic-structure.notes: Chemistry is Dalzell's most credible exponential-speedup territory.

simulation-condensed-matter._sources: Section 5 condensed matter (Hubbard, spin systems). Babbush et al. 2018 Hubbard: 3n logical qubits ~6000, 0.3n^3 Toffoli ~3e9.

margin_tiers._note: Ratio = reported_resource / min_resource. 'far_above' = solidly past the MSA; 'below' = still classically-reachable scale.

_verdict_rules._guidance: Compare (logical_qubits, T-count) against the silo's Minimum Scale for Advantage (MSA). Logic: (1) If no MSA for silo → not_applicable or insufficient_data. (2) If both resources reported and BOTH >= MSA → likely_viable (Dalzell says 'this regime is what end-to-end analysis targets'). (3) If both reported and BOTH below MSA → fails (problem too small — classically trivial). (4) Mixed → conditional. (5) Missing resources → insufficient_data.
